title: Funnel Cake: Crisp Fried Batter Spirals with Icing Sugar and Strawberries
summary: A lacy tangle of light batter fried crisp at 190 °C, dusted with icing sugar and topped with fresh strawberries.
equipment: 23-25 cm heavy pot or deep frying pan
squeeze bottle or jug with a narrow spout (or a funnel)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Whisk the batter
steps.text: Whisk the milk, egg, sugar and vanilla in the bowl, then add the flour, baking powder and salt and whisk until smooth. It should be thick but still pour in a steady ribbon. Rest it for 5 min.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour about 4 cm of oil into the pot and heat to 190 °C. Hot oil sets the thin strands instantly, so they stay crisp rather than oily.

steps.title: Pour the spiral
steps.text: Fill the squeeze bottle with half the batter. Starting at the centre, squeeze it into the oil in a wide spiral, then zigzag back across so the loops join into a cake about 20 cm wide.

steps.title: Fry and flip
steps.text: Fry for 60-90 s until the underside is golden, turn it over with the two fish slices and cook another 60-90 s until crisp and evenly coloured.

steps.title: Make the second cake
steps.text: Drain on the paper, wait until the oil is back at 190 °C, then pour and fry the rest of the batter.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.text: Cut each cake in half, sift over a thick layer of icing sugar and pile on the strawberries. Eat while warm.

tips: A common mistake is batter that is too thick; it forms heavy blobs, so loosen it with 1-2 tsp milk if it will not flow smoothly.
Always let the oil recover to 190 °C between cakes.
Use a pot no wider than 25 cm so the cake keeps a neat round shape.
Any soft fruit or a spoonful of jam works instead of strawberries.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Funnel cake is best eaten within minutes. Leftovers lose their crunch, but you can refresh them in a 200 °C (180 °C fan) oven for 4-5 min.
